_readme: Sources for the culinary journey on uttarpara.html.
EVERY CLAIM IN assets/data/food.js CARRIES A `type` AND A `src` KEY THAT
POINTS INTO `sources` BELOW. The three types are not decoration and they
are the whole reason this file exists:
documented           somebody wrote it down at the time or a named
source records it. State it plainly.
historically-informed  not recorded for Uttarpara specifically, but the
surrounding food history makes it a reasonable
reconstruction. The copy must hedge out loud —
'would likely have', 'a plausible table', 'we can
imagine'. Never state it as fact.
interpretive         our own reading, or a concept for a future menu.
Labelled as such on the page.
`confidence` is for whoever edits this next, not for the reader. It is not
rendered anywhere. It exists so that a future developer does not quietly
promote a medium-confidence reconstruction into a documented fact — which
is precisely how a website ends up teaching a town a history it never had.
WHAT IS NOT IN HERE, AND WILL NOT GO IN WITHOUT EVIDENCE:
· that any dish was invented in Uttarpara
· that Portuguese ships docked at Uttarpara
· any historical person's favourite dish
· that Uttarpara has the best hilsa, or the best fish market, in Bengal
· the name of any Uttarpara sweet shop. Searched; nothing with a
verifiable founding date or history was found. The sweet chapter is
therefore about the custom and names nobody.

municipality.title: Uttarpara-Kotrung Municipality — History of Uttarpara
supports: 1704 settlement by Ratneswar Roychowdhury of the Sabarna Chowdhury family
the area was marshland with fishermen of the Patni and Malo castes, whose trades included fishing and ferrying
Ootarpara was the northern part of the village of Bally
the bridge over the Bally Khal opened 14 February 1846
the English school opened May 1846, part-funded by public subscription
the hospital opened May 1851
the municipality was formed 14 April 1853
named visitors to Uttarpara, described as having visited

wikiTown.title: Wikipedia — Uttarpara
supports: position on the Hooghly opposite Dakshineswar
2011 census population and literacy

sahapedia.title: Sahapedia — Our Food Their Food: A Historical Overview of the Bengali Platter
supports: chillies originated in Central America and spread in India as a substitute for long or black pepper
potatoes reached Europe via the Spanish in 1570; popular in Calcutta by 1860, avoided by orthodox households well into the twentieth century
pineapple in Bengal by 1594
bread and biscuits became contested markers of progress and of caste transgression
the chop adapted the European cutlet by replacing large pieces of meat with small ones
omelette entered Bengali as 'mamlet'
European food advertised in the Calcutta Gazette 1802–1820; Wilson's Auckland Hotel 1841; Peliti's bakery 1881

creoleBengal.title: Confecting Creole Bengal, from Sandesh to Rosogolla: Textural Transformations and Sonic Recall
supports: sandesh and rosogolla are chhana-based and popularly attributed to the Portuguese introduction of milk-curdling to Bengal
the encounter dates to Portuguese settlement in Bengal in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries
sandesh's emergence is placed in 'creole Bengal', when European powers operated in the Hooghly district
rosogolla is popularly credited to Nabin Chandra Das in Calcutta, 1868
creoleBengal.note: The paper describes the Portuguese attribution as a popular attribution and a collective memory, not as settled fact. The page follows that hedge.

chhanaPaper.title: Chhana Sweets of West Bengal: A Culinary Legacy
supports: no mention of chhana in Bengali texts before the sixteenth century
deliberately curdling milk was considered improper in Hindu practice
Portuguese cottage cheese is close to Bengali chhana in method

hilsaHooghly.title: Frontiers in Sustainable Food Systems — Hilsa fisheries in India: fishers in the deltaic Ganga region of river Hooghly
supports: hilsa (Tenualosa ilisha) is a premium table fish for the Bengali community
the major Indian distribution of the species is the Bhagirathi–Hooghly component of the Ganga river system

hooghlyFish.title: Fish diversity in Hooghly district
supports: rohu, mrigel, hilsa, silver carp, lata, koi and pangas are common and in demand in Hooghly district fish markets

vidyasagarWiki.title: Wikipedia — Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar
supports: born Ishwar Chandra Bandyopadhyay, 1820–1891
a childhood of scarcity in Calcutta: household chores after school, studying under street lamps to save lamp oil
vidyasagarWiki.note: No credible source found for a favourite dish. None is claimed.

aurobindoDiet.title: Was Sri Aurobindo a Vegetarian?
supports: he was not vegetarian in early life and still ate meat in Pondicherry into the early 1920s
he gave up meat as the sadhana deepened, not on sentimental grounds
from the ashram's beginning a vegetarian regime was the norm

aurobindoOnFood.title: Sri Aurobindo — on vegetarianism and diet (Auro Society)
supports: his own guidance was that light food sufficient for strength is best and meat not advisable
he held that abstention helps but that the change of consciousness can come without it

saioc.title: Sri Aurobindo Institute — Sri Aurobindo in Calcutta, the Uttarpara speech
supports: 30 May 1909, in the open courtyard on the river side of the library
a year of solitary confinement in the Alipore case preceded it
Amarendranath Chatterjee fetched him from Calcutta

wikiLibrary.title: Wikipedia — Uttarpara Public Library
supports: Michael Madhusudan Dutt stayed two months in 1869 and again in 1873
Vidyasagar and Mary Carpenter visited in 1866
wikiLibrary.note: Records that Madhusudan stayed. Records nothing about what he ate. Nothing is claimed.

wbhc.title: West Bengal Heritage Commission — Uttarpara Jaikrishna Public Library listing
supports: the listing's own wording, 'the first free public library in India', notified 17 January 2008

open_questions: Uttarpara sweet shops: no shop with a verifiable founding date or documented history was found. Named shops need a local source, a plaque, a registration, or the shop itself, before any of them appear on this page.
Uttarpara fish market: the market on Rajendra Avenue is real and hilsa is a Hooghly fish. Whether it is 'the best' anything is an opinion and is written on the page as one.
Michael Madhusudan Dutt's food at Uttarpara: no source located. The card says so.
